text: Why does a broke country get gas
forty times cheaper than the richest country?
Same gas.
This is Doug.
Doug drive snowmobile to work.
Every week, Doug fill the tank.
Doug pay four dollars forty-one a gallon.
In Iran, the same gallon cost eleven cents.
Doug jealous.
Doug want to know why. Three reasons.
Reason one: Iran sit on oil.
Gas come from oil. Oil come from ground.
Iran sit on the third biggest oil pile on Earth.
Oil come out right next door. No ship. No trip.
Reason two: Boss Bear pay.
But oil is not free. Pull it, clean it, ship it. Cost money.
Government sell gas below cost.
So who pay the rest? Boss Bear pay.
Every gallon, Bear pay. Driver pay almost nothing.
That is called a subsidy.
In real life, Iran spends about fifty billion dollars a year to keep energy cheap.
In America, no bear. Doug pay full price. Plus tax.
Reason three: money melt.
Gas price in rials barely move.
But Iran money lost over ninety percent of its value.
So in dollars, gas become pennies.
Doug shocked.
Oil next door. Bear pay. Money melt.
That make Iran the cheapest gas in Asia.
Three cents a liter.
But there is a catch.
Only sixty liters a month at that price.
After that, price double.
Team Iran gas, or team America paycheck?
